Model evaluation

Each sampled task was asked twice: with its image, and without it. Reference answers come from the scene data, never from a model, so a wrong model answer is the model's mistake unless the human audit finds otherwise. Contrast pairs ask the same question about a minimally edited image with a different answer; a model that reads the image gets both right. Sample: 300 of 300 tasks, spread across templates.

Accuracy with the image at each difficulty level. A model breaks at the first level where it answers fewer than 80% right. Every level passes the same gates, so a careful person can answer each task.

Phone photos

300 tasks have a photo twin: the same image seen at a slight angle on a desk, with uneven light, a soft glare, a little blur, sensor noise and JPEG compression. The question and the answer are unchanged; a perspective view keeps which tick a needle points at and what connects to what. The gates were run again on each photo, with the label positions mapped through the same perspective.

Contrast pairs

300 of 300 tasks have a twin: the same question about an image where one thing was edited so the answer changes (a bar, a needle, a cable's end, a valve), and nothing else moves. The median edit is 2% of the scale (the value axis, a dial, a set of ports). Both images pass the same gates. A model that answers from the question text alone can't get both right.

OCR read-back

An independent check of the grounding gate, which trusts the renderer's layout record. Every label a question depends on was cropped out of the final PNG and read by tesseract 5.5.3, an OCR engine unrelated to the models being evaluated. A label counts as read back when the OCR text matches what was drawn (characters OCR commonly confuses, such as O and 0, count as equal). The crops below show what OCR saw.
